procedure.name: swallow_whole_resolution
procedure.condition: A purple worm swallows a creature whole.

steps.step: Creature takes 3d6 damage per round inside the belly.
If the swallowed creature has a sharp weapon, it may attack from inside with a -4 penalty to its attack throw.
Damage stops when either the swallowed creature dies or the worm is killed.
If the swallowed creature dies and remains in the belly for 6 turns, it is irrecoverably digested.

procedure.outcome: Victim is damaged, may attempt internal attacks if equipped, and may be digested permanently after 6 turns if dead.

If the save fails, the weapon is destroyed.

steps.step: The swallowed creature takes 10d10 damage per round from the gizzard.

procedure.outcome: Victim takes ongoing damage, has highly limited counterattack options, and may be digested permanently.

habitat.rule: Can be found in animal waste and other foul refuse.

diet.rule: Prefer to consume tissue that is still alive.

procedure.name: rot_grub_infestation_resolution
procedure.condition: Rot grubs make contact with a living being.

steps.step: Apply fire to the site of contact at once to prevent further burrowing.
Burning a grub inflicts 1d6 points of damage to the character.
If not stopped immediately, the rot grubs reach the heart within 1d3 turns.
When they reach the heart, the victim dies.
The spell cure disease destroys rot grubs in the victim's body.

procedure.outcome: Immediate burning or cure disease can prevent death; otherwise the victim dies within 1d3 turns.

ability.name: magic_item_corrosion
ability.trigger: Magic metal item contacts the antennae or hide.
ability.effect: Magic bonuses are lost 1 at a time until the item becomes ordinary; a later contact then rusts it.
ability.notes: Each current plus grants a 10% probability of surviving contact unscathed.

diet.rule: Feeds upon the rust it creates.

procedure.name: magic_item_corrosion_resolution
procedure.condition: A magical metal item contacts the rust monster's antennae or hide.

steps.step: Determine whether the item survives contact unscathed; its chance equals 10% per current magic bonus.
If the item does not survive contact unscathed, reduce its magic bonus by 1.
Repeat on later contacts until the item becomes ordinary.
After the item becomes ordinary, any subsequent contact rusts it into uselessness.

procedure.outcome: Magic items lose bonuses incrementally and are eventually destroyed.
